```bash
#!/bin/bash

# Date format tool - formats date strings according to format specification
# Usage: date-format <date_string> <format_string>

if [ $# -ne 2 ]; then
    echo "Usage: date-format <date_string> <format_string>" >&2
    exit 1
fi

date_input="$1"
format_string="$2"

# Parse the input date - handle different separators
year=$(echo "$date_input" | sed 's/[/-]/ /g' | awk '{print $1}')
month=$(echo "$date_input" | sed 's/[/-]/ /g' | awk '{print $2}')
day=$(echo "$date_input" | sed 's/[/-]/ /g' | awk '{print $3}')

# Validate input
if [ -z "$year" ] || [ -z "$month" ] || [ -z "$day" ]; then
    echo "Error: Invalid date format" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Ensure 2-digit formatting for month and day
month_formatted=$(printf "%02d" "$month")
day_formatted=$(printf "%02d" "$day")

# Replace format placeholders
result="$format_string"
result=$(echo "$result" | sed "s/%Y/$year/g")
result=$(echo "$result" | sed "s/%m/$month_formatted/g")
result=$(echo "$result" | sed "s/%d/$day_formatted/g")

echo "$result"
EOF
```
